title: PRD Control Plane package update and restart for managed repos
specification:
# PRD: Control Plane package update and restart for managed repos

## Problem
Managed repos that run the Autonomy v2 control bridge and server do not have a Control Plane workflow to pull the newest published `@asalaza6/autonomy-v2` package, install it, and restart their local bridge/server processes. The UI also does not clearly show each repo’s currently installed Autonomy v2 package version.

## Goal
After this repo publishes a new patch release, each managed repo can independently detect or receive an update request, install the newest Autonomy v2 package, refresh scaffold/config, restart its bridge and server, and report the installed version back to the Control Plane UI.

## Requirements
- Keep `npm run release:patch` as the release path for publishing this repo to npm.
- Add a Control Plane job type such as `package:update` for a specific repo.
- Extend the bridge to claim `package:update` jobs for mapped repos.
- Reuse or wrap `autonomy-v2 update --root <repo>` so managed repos install `@asalaza6/autonomy-v2@latest` with their detected package manager.
- After update, restart the local `autonomy-v2-control bridge` process and the `autonomy-v2-server` process when they are running under a supported supervisor or configured restart command.
- Add config for restart commands, for example `controlBridgeRestartCommand` and `serverRestartCommand`, with safe no-op behavior when not configured.
- Report update result fields: previous declared version, new declared version, installed version, package manager, refresh status, restart status, and errors.
- Add installed Autonomy v2 package version to repo status snapshots, independent of deploy/build version.
- Show that version dynamically in the Control Plane repo page using the current installed package version from the managed repo.
- Do not auto-update every repo without explicit job/user action unless an auto-update setting is added and enabled per repo.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A manager can queue an update job for one managed repo from the Control Plane.
- The repo’s bridge installs the latest `@asalaza6/autonomy-v2`, refreshes init, and completes the job with structured result data.
- If restart commands are configured, bridge/server restart is attempted and reflected in the job result.
- If restart commands are missing, the update succeeds and reports restart as skipped, not failed.
- The repo page displays the installed Autonomy v2 package version dynamically from the latest repo status.
- Existing deploy version UI remains separate from package version UI.
- Existing `deploy`, `prd:add`, and `agent:chat` jobs continue to work.

## Verification
- Unit test update job creation, validation, claiming, and completion.
- Bridge test proving `package:update` invokes the update path and returns installed version data.
- Test skipped restart behavior when restart commands are not configured.
- Test configured restart command execution and error reporting.
- UI/dashboard test proving installed package version renders from repo status.
- Run `npm run typecheck` and relevant unit tests.
